summary: Specifies the procedure for registering RTP payload formats as media types, using audio, video, or other media subtype names. This lets text-based descriptions or control protocols identify what an RTP stream contains. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC explains how to register a media type that names an RTP payload format. It also shows how the media type's information maps into an SDP session description.

questions: how to register an rtp payload format
how does a media type map to sdp
what information goes in an rtp media type registration
subtitle: The registration rules for naming RTP payload formats as media types and mapping them into SDP.

tldr.problem: Text-based session descriptions and control protocols need a standard name for the media format carried by an RTP transmission.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds RTP-specific requirements to the general media type registration template, including clock-rate and packet-time parameters and a mapping to SDP.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4855 obsoletes RFC 3555 and defines no registrations itself. It is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 8851.

today: RFC 4855 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3555 and has been updated by RFC 8851.

sections.title: What an RTP Media Type Identifies
sections.content:
RFC 4288 defines general procedures for registering media types with IANA. RFC 4855 adds requirements for media types that identify payload formats carried by the Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP).

A registered type gives a text-based description or control protocol a standard way to identify the format of an RTP transmission. The RFC defines the procedure; it does not register individual types.
sections.plainLanguage: A registered media type gives a standard name to the format carried in an RTP stream. This RFC explains the extra information needed when registering that kind of name.

sections.title: Information in a Registration
sections.content:
Registration follows the general template in RFC 4288, with added RTP details. A rate parameter is required if the payload format has no fixed RTP timestamp clock rate. Audio formats may include channels; formats may also specify ptime and maxptime for the amount of media represented in a packet.

The registration must describe encoding considerations and state that the media type is defined for RTP transfer, especially when it depends on RTP framing. Its published specification must include the RTP timestamp clock rate. New optional parameters may be added to an existing RTP media type only if they do not change existing behavior and older implementations can ignore them.

The RFC covers new types, existing non-RTP types extended to RTP, and RTP types extended to non-RTP transfer. In each case, parameters must say which transfer mode they apply to.
sections.plainLanguage: A registration must describe the clock rate and how the payload is carried. It must also distinguish parameters for RTP from parameters for other transfer methods.

sections.title: Example Registration
sections.content:
The RFC shows a fictional type called audio/example. The example's required rate is its sampling rate, with 8000 as a typical value. Its optional channels parameter defaults to 1 when omitted and may be 1 for mono or 2 for stereo.

The sample also says that the format is framed binary data and depends on RTP framing. Its references to RFC nnnn are placeholders for the RFC that would specify the payload format.
sections.plainLanguage: The example uses a made-up audio type to show the fields a registration should contain. Its values illustrate the template rather than define a real payload format.

sections.title: Sharing a Subtype Name
sections.content:
The same subtype name must not be used for RTP and non-RTP transfer unless the data format is the same. For this purpose, a file format may equal the concatenated RTP payloads without the RTP header or payload-format header. A file may still contain a magic number or other header that RTP does not carry.

The required parameters must also be the same for both transfer methods. If the format or required parameters differ, the registrations must use separate types. The RFC suggests related subtype names and proposes +rtp as a suffix for the RTP form.
sections.plainLanguage: A type name can cover both a file and an RTP payload only when their data formats and required parameters match. Otherwise, they need separate, preferably related, names.

sections.title: Mapping Media Types to SDP
sections.content:
Session Description Protocol (SDP) describes RTP sessions using fields that correspond to parts of a media type. The media type, such as audio, maps to the m= media name. The subtype maps to the encoding name in a=rtpmap.

The rate and channels parameters also map to a=rtpmap. The ptime and maxptime parameters map to their corresponding SDP attributes. Payload-format-specific parameters go in a=fmtp, and the payload format specification defines which are allowed.
sections.plainLanguage: SDP places each part of the media type in a defined field. This lets the session description identify the media and its RTP encoding parameters.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The registration procedure itself does not create security risks, but the media type being registered may have risks. Active content can cause harmful actions, audio or video can hide data, and compressed data can expand to consume resources. RTP security is addressed in RFC 3550.

Every registration must state applicable security considerations and identify known risks. A claim that no risks exist must not be confused with saying that risks have not been assessed.
sections.plainLanguage: A media type's label does not make its content safe. Each registration must describe known risks and distinguish an assessment with no known issues from an assessment that has not been done.

viz.caption: EXAMPLE MEDIA TYPE AND SDP MAPPING FROM RFC 4855

data.title: L16 audio example
data.code:
audio/L16; rate=48000; channels=2; ptime=5; emphasis=50-15

m=audio 49170 RTP/AVP 97
a=rtpmap:97 L16/48000/2
a=fmtp:97 emphasis=50-15
a=ptime:5
